- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially for the first 5–10 days; model tends to be too optimistic after recent spikes.
- Underestimate sharp downward moves or sudden drops (e.g., 34.33, 33.70) — model fails to capture volatility in low-price zones.
- Overshoot after high peaks (e.g., 44.49 → 44.07, 45.93 → 43.55) — model overreacts to recent highs, fails to mean-revert.
- Lag in response to true price drops — model often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward after a true drop.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect upward after a dip, then undercorrect downward after a spike.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently underestimate the true mean, especially in the middle of the horizon (days 10–20).
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends; model overfits short-term momentum, underestimates structural breaks or policy shocks.
